title: Why sleep is the best medicine
text:
We all know the feeling: after a bad night, it's hard to concentrate, we feel irritable and even simple tasks seem difficult. Yet many of us still treat sleep as something we can cut when life gets busy. Scientists say this is a big mistake.

Most adults need between seven and nine hours of sleep a night. Teenagers need even more, because their bodies and brains are still developing. However, surveys suggest that a large number of people regularly sleep less than seven hours.

While we sleep, our body is far from inactive. The brain sorts and stores the information we collected during the day, which is why a good night's sleep before an exam can be more useful than studying until 3 a.m. Sleep also helps the body repair itself and fight infections. People who sleep badly for a long time are more likely to have problems with their heart, their weight and their mood.

So what can we do to sleep better? Experts give some simple advice. Try to go to bed and get up at the same time every day, even at weekends. Avoid coffee in the afternoon and large meals late in the evening. Keep your bedroom cool, dark and quiet. And perhaps most importantly, put your phone away at least an hour before bed. The light from screens tells the brain that it is still daytime, and scrolling through social media keeps our minds busy when they should be slowing down.

If you still can't sleep after twenty minutes, doctors suggest getting up and doing something relaxing, like reading a paper book, until you feel sleepy. Lying in bed and worrying about not sleeping usually makes things worse.
